question: Is the documented fail-closed `update_partial` plus status/Doctor/fresh-plan recovery contract acceptable for the first experimental mutation release, or must immutable operation identity and reconciliation land before any consented apply command?
rationale: The code intentionally cannot make external package, source-config, and Gateway mutations atomic; choosing the acceptable recovery guarantee is a product and operator-safety decision, not a mechanical patch correction.

options.title: Require live recovery proof for the bounded contract
options.body: Require exact-head redacted evidence of package replacement, Gateway cron convergence/retry, and retained-artifact recovery, then decide whether the documented experimental recovery flow is sufficient.

options.title: Require reconciliation before apply ships
options.body: Defer the mutation command until immutable operation identity and a Doctor/retry/reconcile path can resolve uncertain external operations.

options.title: Keep update read-only for now
options.body: Land or retain only the planner behavior and postpone consented mutation until the lifecycle stack has maintainer-approved recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Require live recovery proof for the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Require exact-head redacted evidence of package replacement, Gateway cron convergence/retry, and retained-artifact recovery, then decide whether the documented experimental recovery flow is sufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete review criteria for uncertain compensation and operator recovery on this exact PR.
